hypothesis: A poisoned bind-time socket identity can cause an exiting owner to unlink a successor’s live socket; tombstoned adoption must not trust a foreign listener at the dead worker pathname.
approach: Own and close the supervisor/worker listener before exit cleanup; probe liveness then apply identity-gated unlink. Add fail-first poisoned-capture e2e tests. For tombstoned adoption, compare recorded pid/start identity before socket auth and share a one-second force-stop deadline across auth plus route. Add silent-listener impostor regression.
parity_notes: TS daemon-mode.ts:8011-8018 and daemon-supervisor.ts:7436-7491 close server before cleanup. TS cleanupDaemonSocketPath checks identity alone and can unlink a successor after a poisoned bind-time capture; Rust post-close live-listener probe deliberately exceeds TS to protect this race. TS adoptOrRecoverWorker checks recorded PID; TS stopWorker(force) bounds IPC to one second. No user-facing behavior changed. Socket inode alone is not a reliable owner proof after replacement.
